text: Ungodly children are worthless and are nothing to desire or to celebrate.
You can have lots of children, but they will bring joy only if they fear the Lord.
Having lots of ungodly children won't help you in old age— you will outlive them all. One good child, or even no children at all, is better than a thousand who are ungodly.
A family that disobeys the law can make a city a ghost town, but one smart person can fill an empty city with people.
Here are but a few of the important things I have seen and heard:
If a small group of sinners sets the Lord's anger ablaze, then it will be worse by far if a whole nation is sinful.
Long ago, the Lord refused to forgive the mighty giants who rebelled against him.
And he so hated the arrogance of the people of Sodom,[28] that he destroyed them.
They were doomed because of their sins, and the Lord showed no mercy as he swept them away.
Nor did he have pity on six hundred thousand stubborn Assyrian soldiers who attacked his people.

Even if only one person refused to obey the Lord, I would be surprised if he did not punish that one. The Lord loves to show mercy and to use his mighty power to forgive his people, but when his anger overflows against sinners,
he uses that same power to punish them. Everyone will receive either mercy or punishment as each deserves.
The Lord refuses to let sinners profit from their crimes, and he will reward his people if they patiently wait.
He remembers every good deed and gives everyone what they deserve.
The Lord wanted everyone to know his mighty power, so he put a stubborn heart in the king of Egypt.
But the Lord also wants everyone to know about his mercy, so he separated those who have his light from those who remain in darkness.[29]
Never say to yourself, “The Lord cannot see me. He doesn't even know my name. There are just too many people for him to keep me in mind.
One glance from him causes quaking and shaking in the earth and the sky, in the highest heaven and the deepest sea,
in the mountains and the foundations of the earth.
But no human can understand how his mighty power works.
Most of what God does cannot be seen, just like the wind in a violent storm.
So who will tell him when I do what is right? And who has the patience to wait for him to keep his promises?”
That is how fools speak— they cannot think straight and have no understanding.
Listen, students; pay attention, and you will learn.
I will train you and tell you exactly what I know.
In the beginning, when the Lord created the world, he gave each thing its proper place.
He designed the forces of nature to last for all time— they never tire or get hungry or stop working.
They don't get in the way of each other, and they will never disobey him.
After God created the earth, he looked it over and filled it with creatures that were good;
animals of all kinds covered the ground, and when they die, they return to it.
